findings.text: Gzip member decoder that accepts either a resident input image or a refill callback and either a caller output area or a drain callback, with optional consumed input accounting and a failure reporter, signalling success with zero and any failure with negative status while releasing all transient allocations.
Thin wrapper that forwards its input, refill, drain, output, position and failure arguments to the gzip member decoder while requesting unbounded output length handling.
Thin wrapper that forwards input, refill, drain, output with explicit length, position and failure arguments to the gzip member decoder.

LZ4 archive decoder that consumes a sequence of length prefixed blocks framed by a magic marker, accepting either resident input or a refill callback and either a resident output cursor or a drain callback, tracking logical input consumption and reporting failures through a caller callback with zero on success and negative on failure.
Wrapper that invokes the LZ4 archive decoder after reserving trailing bytes that carry the total uncompressed length used in early boot mode.

LZMA stream decoder that parses a packed header, derives coder and position parameters, builds probability tables, then emits exactly the declared destination size through either a resident buffer or a dictionary sized staging buffer with drain callback, reporting consumed input and success status.
Wrapper that invokes the LZMA decoder after reserving trailing bytes from the supplied input length.

A candidate gzip member is rejected unless at least ten bytes are available with leading wire values for gzip and deflate method, after which ten bytes are skipped and an optional zero terminated name field is skipped without refilling, treating exhaustion during that skip as corruption.

When a drain callback exists a fixed internal output staging area is obtained, otherwise the caller area is used with a fallback that treats a zero length as effectively unlimited, while input either reuses the caller image or obtains a staging buffer and the codec state plus workspace are always transiently held with window retention only when draining.
On success or header rejection the optional position slot is updated, with the success value accounting for consumed input plus trailer bytes skipped beyond the codec input cursor.

The LZ4 stream must open with a four byte marker, repeated markers denote alignment padding and are skipped, a zero block length terminates the stream in resident input mode, otherwise each block length is followed by that many payload bytes, and the optional position accumulates header bytes plus decoded payload lengths.

Resident input and refill callback are mutually exclusive and one must be present, as are resident output and drain callback with staging areas obtained when callbacks supply data movement, and oversized block declarations beyond the bound for the maximum uncompressed chunk are rejected in refill mode.

In early boot mode the decoder trims each output request to the remaining total taken from the stream tail and uses an unchecked fast path, while the other build uses a bounded safe path limited to the maximum chunk size, with negative decode results treated as corruption.

The LZMA decoder reads a packed header of properties plus dictionary and destination sizes, rejects property values at or above the product bound, splits the value into literal, position and length components with derived bit masks, converts multi byte fields from little endian order, and coerces a zero dictionary size to one.

Probability storage is sized from a fixed base plus a literal area scaled by the sum of literal and position bits, held transiently, then initialised over the literal inclusive prefix to half of the model total before decoding begins.

The range decoder starts with all one bits in range and zero code, primes code from five input bytes refilling as needed, defaults to a failing refill when none is supplied, and treats refill exhaustion during priming or normalisation as unexpected end of input.

Each binary decision normalises when range falls below a threshold by shifting in one byte, derives a bound from the stored probability scaled by range, then moves range and code to the selected subinterval while nudging the probability toward the observed outcome with a fixed shift.

Output position is the sum of a flushed global count and a staging offset, writes advance the staging cursor and remember the last byte, reaching dictionary capacity triggers a full dictionary drain and wrap when draining, and backward references wrap modulo dictionary size with different handling for resident versus draining modes.

Decoding proceeds until emitted bytes reach the declared destination size, aborting as corrupt on literal or match step failure, stopping early on an explicit end marker distance, and finally draining any staged tail with exact length match required when draining.
Early boot selection is indicated by a marker defined in each of the decompressors, and a minimum helper selects the smaller of two values for staging sizing.

Gzip states cycle among header validation, codec initialisation, input refill when exhausted, block decode, conditional staging drain, and terminal success on stream end versus terminal failure on read, write or codec error, with deterministic release of workspace, state, and any owned buffers on all exits.

LZ4 states cycle among initial marker check, block header fetch, padding skip, payload fetch, decode, optional drain with cursor advance, and termination on empty refill, zero length in resident mode, or input exhaustion, with owned staging released on all exits.

The match history holds a state index plus four recent distances, literals reset or step the state down through defined bands while matches step it up, short repeats emit one byte and long paths decode length then optionally distance with validation against dictionary and emitted size before copying.
Range decoder state groups a refill callback and failure reporter with buffer base, cursor, end and last size, plus current code, range and bound words used by normalisation and binary decisions.
Packed header layout holds an eight bit property field followed by a thirty two bit dictionary size and a sixty four bit destination size with no padding.

Output staging state groups a byte buffer and capacity with last byte memory, staging offset, flushed global count, optional drain callback, and a back pointer to the parsed header for dictionary sizing.
History state holds a small integer coder state plus four unsigned recent distance registers initialised to one.

Every transient allocation failure is reported through the caller failure callback and unwinds only already owned resources in reverse order, with ownership conditional on whether caller images or callbacks were supplied.

Short input, bad magic, name overrun, codec errors, invalid LZ4 headers, truncated blocks, negative decode results, bad LZMA properties, and out of range distances all report through the failure callback and yield negative status without partial success.

Negative refill results and short drains are treated as read and write failures respectively, refill returning zero terminates LZ4 cleanly at block boundaries but is unexpected inside range decoder refill, and final tail drains must match exactly.
LZ4 framed streams use a thirty two bit little endian marker with hexadecimal value 184C2102 to open the stream and to denote padding blocks.
Maximum uncompressed bytes per LZ4 block in these fragments is eight mebibytes, expressed as eight shifted left by twenty.
LZMA staged input uses sixty four kibibytes, hexadecimal 10000, as the refill quantum.
Range coder uses top threshold twenty four bits, probability shift five bits, and model total eleven bits.

Gzip handling observes a ten byte minimum header with leading values 1F 8B and method 08, a name present flag bit 08 in the fourth byte, a thirty two kibibyte staging size 8000 hex when draining, and an eight byte trailer skipped in position accounting.
LZMA model uses base size 1846, literal size 768, maximum position bits 4, low and mid length bits 3 each, high length bits 8, twelve states with seven literal states, and minimum match length 2.
LZMA position model uses start index 4, end index 14, full distance count derived as one shifted by half the end index, six slot bits, four length to position states, and four align bits.

Probability table layout orders match, repeat, repeat distance, long repeat, slot, special position, align, length and repeat length groups before literals, with length subgroups for choice, low, mid and high derived from position and length bit counts.
